subject: Prometheus2b decode stalls causing elevated 504s — interim mitigations & follow-up
messages:
From: Jared Klein <jared.k@optimolabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Prometheus2b decode stalls — errors in production

Hi Ben —

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 504 / timeout errors from calls hitting Prometheus2b around 08:50 PST this morning (Nov 4). The errors look concentrated on long-context chat sessions and there are multiple requests returning immediate 504s.

Attached is a short sample of request ids and HTTP traces (prometheus2b-error-snippets.txt). Affected requests are from our primary inference route (route id: optimo-prod-gen). Our consumers are reporting degraded UX; one large batch job also failed.

Can you confirm whether this is a known degradation or if you need more signal from our side? We can provide additional request ids, approximate prompt sizes, or stack traces from the client.

Thanks —
Jared Klein
Director of Platform
Optimo Labs
Attachment: prometheus2b-error-snippets.txt (text, 24 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jared Klein <jared.k@optimolabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 09:30:15 -0800
Subject: Re: Prometheus2b decode stalls — errors in production

Jared — thanks for the heads up and for the snippets. We're seeing a matching spike on our side in Prometheus2b's 5xx-rate starting ~08:48 PST. Looping in Ops (Marissa) and Platform Eng (Rafael) to triage immediately.

Immediate ask: can you paste 2–3 full request ids (same format as in the attachment) and the largest prompt length for the failing calls? That will help us map to the serving shard and kernel path.

Initial mitigation we can try while we triage: route your traffic that normally goes to Prometheus2b to the Prometheus1b fallback pool (lower-capacity but different runtime path) and reduce max_tokens to 512 for the next 30–60 mins to reduce decode pressure. If you're OK with that, we'll flip routing and monitor error rates.

I'll keep you updated every hour until we have stability.

—Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Klein <jared.k@optimolabs.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 10:05:40 -0800
Subject: Prometheus2b decode stalls — triage notes and temporary mitigations

Team / Jared — quick triage summary and the set of mitigations we're applying now (10:05 PST):

1) What we're seeing
- Prometheus2b shows elevated 504 rates (decode stage) starting 08:48 PST, peaking ~09:10. Error signature looks like stalled token decode rather than model OOMs; kernels hit a slow path when prompt-length + streaming flag are both high.
- Error rate concentrated on requests with prompt_size > ~18k tokens and open streaming connections.

2) Immediate mitigations (applied):
- Enabled per-customer route throttling for Optimo Labs to limit concurrent streams to 8 (from 40).
- Short-term routing: shifted 40% of Optimo-prod-gen traffic to Prometheus1b fallback pool (non-streaming optimized path) — this is a gradual shift to avoid cold caches.
- Enforced caller-side max_tokens cap: we pushed a config that trims max_tokens to 512 for requests flagged as long-context. Please note this is temporary and opt-in on your side if you prefer us to only do routing.
- Added a short-circuit for requests exceeding 95s decode time to fail fast and fall back to Prometheus1b.

3) Next steps we're executing now
- Rafael to capture trace-level kernel metrics and a KV-cache hit/miss report for the affected time window (INFRA-4523).
- Running a quick binary search on quantization kernels to isolate whether a specific kernel version correlates with stalls.
- Preparing mitigation-runbook-v1.pdf (internal runbook + customer FAQ) and attaching for reference.

4) Customer impact & ask
- We expect visible error-rate reduction within 20–40 minutes after routing and concurrency throttles.
- Jared: if you can provide 5–10 example request ids with timestamps (local client time), we will map them to server traces and include per-request RCA snippets in our postmortem.

I'll post an ops update in INFRA-4523 in ~1 hour with kernel traces and a short timeline.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Klein <jared.k@optimolabs.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 12:16:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Prometheus2b decode stalls — triage notes and temporary mitigations

Thanks — quick engineering notes from the platform side:

- Kernel correlation: initial sampling shows a 2.1x longer median decode step for the K-quant-v7 path under streaming compared with non-streaming. We're reproducing locally with a long append-only prompt and streaming enabled.
- KV-cache contention: a small subset of shards shows elevated lock contention when many concurrent streaming sessions attempt prefix fetches; this exacerbates latency, causing upstream HTTP timeouts.

Planned technical mitigations (in progress):
- Backpressure change: we'll adaptively prioritize KV-prefetch for active sessions and fall back to on-demand fetch for cold prefixes (reduces contention). Rolling this change as a narrow flag to Prometheus2b by 14:00 PST.
- Kernel rollback: if the adaptive prefetch flag does not reduce stalls in the next hour, we'll revert to K-quant-v6 on the impacted shards and keep the routing fallback in place.
- Postmortem ETA: drafting full RCA and action items; target delivery to Optimo by 2027-11-09 COB.

Jared — thanks for sending the request ids earlier. We'll include per-request server traces in the RCA (with your permission).

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Subject: Prometheus2b decode stalls — current status and next steps

Jared / Sofia — final update for today and the asks we have from Optimo: 

Status (16:30 PST):
- Error rate for Prometheus2b related 504s is back to baseline for Optimo-prod-gen (observed 94% reduction in 5xxs vs peak). The routing + concurrency throttles plus the adaptive-kv-prefetch flag materially reduced stalls.
- We will keep the 40% traffic split to Prometheus1b for the next 12 hours while we stabilize and validate the kernel change.

What you might notice
- For long-context streaming calls you may see slightly slower first-token latencies during the split window while caches warm on Prometheus1b fallback; overall success rate should be restored.

Deliverables and timeline
- Short incident postmortem (1–2 pages) with per-request traces for the ids you provided: ETA 2027-11-06 EOD.
- Full RCA and permanent mitigations: ETA 2027-11-09 COB. This will include an action plan for: better prefetch isolation, improved kernel gating, and an observability dashboard for early-detect on decode path slowdowns.

Customer ask / permissions
- Jared: to include per-request server traces in our RCA, we need Optimo's permission to share sanitized traces that contain request ids and timings (no PII). Please reply to this thread with a quick approval or a range of request-ids you prefer excluded.

Attachments and links
- mitigation-runbook-v1.pdf (attached) — contains customer-visible FAQ and a short rollback/playbook.
- Internal ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4523
- Shared RCA folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Prometheus2b-RCA

Thanks again for patience and for sending the request ids — the team will keep monitoring overnight and Rafael will post kernel traces to INFRA-4523 in the morning.

—Ben
